ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brown with a dark lateral band and pale dorsal markings. Males display a distinctive foot-flagging behavior near forest streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus silvaticus* is best distinguished by its distinct, cream-colored, hourglass-shaped dorsal marking, which contrasts sharply against its dark brown body.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus silvaticus* inhabits the leaf litter and rocky stream banks of evergreen tropical forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,000m.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus silvaticus* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, rhythmically extending and waving their hind legs to signal in noisy forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus silvaticus* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon. Females deposit small clutches of eggs in hidden, subterranean nests within stream beds.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus silvaticus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Forest Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, rapid series of short, insect-like chirps while perched on rocks near fast-flowing forest streams.
